name: Scoreboard
intent: A strip of key numbers at the top of a screen, like open invoices, revenue or overdue amount, each with an optional trend and spark chart.
usage: Use Scoreboard for the 3 to 6 numbers that sum up a screen. It is one component: pass items as data. Each item is a card with a title, the metric, and optional badge, metadata line, trend (arrow, value and unit, colored by status) and spark chart (a small line drawn from points). Cards share the width and run side by side with no gap; every card but the last has a thin line down its right side, the full height of the card. selectable turns each card into a button: picking one marks it selected, like a filter for the list below, and picking it again clears it. Past four cards the Scoreboard puts itself in a Conveyor, so arrows at both ends move the row; the arrows show only when the cards do not fit. See contracts/scoreboard.json for the full contract. On a box narrower than 640px, the kit's mobile break, the cards take a smaller minimum so two are in view, the strip snaps card by card, and the Conveyor's arrows give way to swiping.

items.itemShape: { id: string; title: string; metric: string; metadata?: string; badge?: string; trend?: { value: string; unit?: string; status?: "success" | "danger" | "neutral"; direction?: "up" | "down" | "none" }; chart?: { points: number[]; status?: "success" | "danger" | "neutral"; area?: boolean } }
items.note: 3 to 6 cards. badge is a neutral Badge next to the title. trend status is good (success), bad (danger) or neutral; direction none drops the arrow and goes with status neutral. chart points are drawn left to right; its status defaults to the trend's, and area (default true) fills under the line.

selectable.note: Cards become buttons that show hover and selected states.

selected.note: Controlled id of the selected card, or null for none.

defaultSelected.note: Starting selection when selected is not controlled.

onSelectedChange.note: (id: string | null) => void. Picking the selected card again passes null.

scroll.note: The row scrolls when it does not fit, and past four cards a Conveyor with arrows does it. Turn it off when the Scoreboard is already inside your own Conveyor.

label.note: Names the strip for screen readers.

useWhen: The top of a list or dashboard screen, to sum it up in a few numbers.
Numbers that filter the list below: make it selectable.
More than four numbers: they stay in one strip, which the Conveyor moves along.
doNot: Do not build a metric row from your own divs or cards, or add a MetricCard, ScoreCard or Sparkline. Pass items.
Do not use the chart as a real chart; it only shows the shape of the trend. Use a chart for readable data.
Do not pair direction none with a success or danger status.
Do not split one set of numbers into two strips. Keep them in one, and let the Conveyor move it.
a11y: A group named by label. Each card reads its title, metric, trend and metadata in order.
The trend arrow is read as Up or Down before the value, so color is not the only signal.
The spark chart is an image named by its direction, like Trend going up.
When selectable, each card is a button with aria-pressed and a visible focus ring.
On a phone-width box the arrows are gone but the strip is still a focus stop, so the arrow keys move it.
When plain cards scroll sideways, the strip becomes a focus stop named by label, so the arrow keys scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1). Selectable cards are buttons, so the strip adds no stop.
snippet:
<Scoreboard
  items={[
    { id: "open", title: "Open invoices", metric: "128", badge: "This month", trend: { value: "12%", unit: "MoM", status: "success", direction: "up" }, metadata: "Updated today" },
    { id: "revenue", title: "Revenue", metric: "$482,900", chart: { points: [52, 58, 54, 66, 62, 74, 70, 82], status: "success" }, metadata: "Last 8 weeks" },
    { id: "overdue", title: "Overdue", metric: "$36,420", trend: { value: "4.1%", unit: "MoM", status: "danger", direction: "up" }, metadata: "14 accounts" },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: Trends
examples.usage: Each card with a badge, a trend and a metadata line. Green for good, red for bad, gray for no change.

examples.title: Spark charts
examples.usage: chart draws the points as a small line with a fill under it, colored like its status.

examples.title: Selectable
examples.usage: Cards are buttons. Hover shows a line under the card; the selected card turns blue. Pick it again to clear it.

examples.title: Six cards
examples.usage: Up to 6 cards share the width. Narrow screens scroll the strip sideways.
